triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module capped the section 22 credit with two rules (`elderly_disabled_preceding_credits`, a hand-listed sum of foreign tax credit, CDCC, AOTC, LLC, saver's, and two residential energy credits, and `elderly_disabled_credit_credit_limit`) whose own `source` fields cite IRS Schedule 3 credit ordering rather than anything in 26 USC 22, so the encoding carried a limitation branch with no basis in the cited provision.
triage.triage_notes: The quote is the removed `source:` line on `elderly_disabled_preceding_credits`; the companion removed rule carried `source: Credit against tax imposed by this chapter; IRS Schedule 3 ordering`. Both rules are deleted and the post-fix output is simply `section_22_amount * section_22_credit_rate` when eligible. Two further fidelity gains in the same diff that a reviewer could prefer as the headline: (a) the 22(c)(3)(A) reduction was rewritten from three generic received-minus-taxable differences to the statute's enumerated categories (title II Social Security Act, Railroad Retirement Act of 1974, VA-administered, any other non-title exclusion) and now adds the 22(c)(3)(B) workmen's-compensation clause ('any amount treated as a social security benefit under section 86(d)(3)'), which was entirely absent pre-fix — that part is unrepresented_clause; (b) `section_22_initial_amount_cap` was rewritten from `aged_count * 5000 + under_65_disability_income` to the actual 22(c)(2)(B) structure (no cap when all qualified individuals are 65+, $5,000 + the under-65 spouse's disability income on a joint return with one aged spouse, otherwise the disability-income cap). Also the aggregation relation changed from an unconstrained `elderly_disabled_member_of_tax_unit` to `taxpayer_or_spouse_of_tax_unit`, which narrows a scope the pre-fix module had only asserted in a prose comment. Provision text for 26 USC 22 was read only through the module's added verbatim summary, not a separate resolver call.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module capped the credit with `min(elderly_disabled_credit_credit_limit, elderly_disabled_credit_potential)`, where the limit was `max(0, income_tax_before_credits - elderly_disabled_preceding_credits)` over a hand-listed set (foreign tax credit, CDCC, AOTC, LLC, saver's, and two residential energy credits) whose own `source` fields say "IRS Schedule 3 ordering" rather than anything in the module's cited provision. I read 26 USC 22 (a)-(f) through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-07-13, body sha256 01c0c846...): it contains no credit-ordering rule, no tax-liability cap, and no reference to any of those seven credits, so the pre-fix encoding carried a limitation branch with no basis in the cited source. The fix deletes both rules and re-grounds `elderly_disabled_credit` on 22(a) as `section_22_amount * section_22_credit_rate`, and the companion test drops the `income_tax_before_credits`/seven-credit inputs and the `elderly_disabled_credit_credit_limit: 5000` assertion, so the removal was deliberate, not incidental reformatting. The section 26(a) limitation it was imitating already lives in its own module (`statutes/26/26.yaml`, rule `income_tax_capped_non_refundable_credits`, present at both parent and fix commits), which makes the 22-module branch both ungrounded and duplicative — squarely "a formula grounded on the wrong provision."

(2) "It is incidental to a wholesale regeneration" — the test file change independently confirms intent. (3) "A different kind fits better" — untraceable_branch fits the flagged rule_path best. Caveat for the reviewer: this module diff carries at least two other independent fidelity deltas that a single label will not capture, so if the corpus wants one case per defect it may be worth splitting. Those are (a) `section_22_married_filing_requirement_satisfied`, pre `filing_status != 2 or spouses_lived_apart_all_year` vs post `not married_at_close_of_taxable_year or filing_status == 1 or spouses_lived_apart_all_year` — the pre-fix gate let a married-but-not-joint filer in any status other than MFS take the credit, which 22(e)(1) forbids (unrepresented_clause / polarity_or_logic); and (b) `section_22_nontaxable_pension_benefit_reduction`, re-grounded from generic received-minus-taxable terms onto the enumerated 22(c)(3)(A) sources plus the previously absent 22(c)(3)(B) section 86(d)(3) workers-compensation clause (unrepresented_clause). The `section_22_initial_amount_cap` rewrite, by contrast, is behaviorally near-equivalent to the pre-fix `(aged_count * 5000) + under_65_disability_income` and should not be counted as a separate defect. The commit body is empty and the PR (#25) is about 26 USC 63(c), so the commit/PR text gives no independent corroboration; all weight here is on the diff, the test diff, and the pinned source text.
